$comment: RAG module I/O contract, version 1: what the middleware sends the RAG module and what it gets back. JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) so any language validates the same bytes. Two extension keywords: `x-enum-from: <field>` means 'the closed enum of that field in rag_metadata.v1.json' — referenced, never copied, so the two contracts cannot drift; `x-status` is `live` (the RAG module reads it today) or `planned` (accepted and validated, not yet acted on). A field marked live that nothing reads is a test failure — a contract nothing honours is worse than none, because people trust it. Versioning follows rag_metadata: adding an optional field = minor bump; renaming, removing or tightening = major bump and a new file. `locked: false` until the middleware owner signs off the request shape.

request.description: One retrieval request. Sent once per brief — the result is frozen into the prompt prefix the draft, judge and revise calls share.

contract_version.description: The version of this file the caller built the request against.

run_id.description: Correlates this request with the brief run, its trace and the CLAN file.

research.description: Findings already selected from category / brand research (Postgres), with their ids — not raw documents. Used by the validation stage as extra query context and to avoid returning what the model already has.

attachments.description: Text of documents the user added. UNTRUSTED: may shape the validation query, may never set scope, tenant or brand.

authority.description: Who this run is FOR. Injected by the middleware from the session and the campaign record — never computed by the RAG module, never taken from document text (foundation-spec M3). This object is the confidentiality boundary.

tenant.description: The agency. Unlocks that agency's own material; null = licensed house corpus only.

brand.description: The authorised SUBJECT brand, snake_case. The only thing that unlocks brand-scoped material. null = category and global material only.

references.description: Other brands named in the brief. Every role here is PUBLIC MATERIAL ONLY, even when the brand is also a client — role decides data scope, and only authority.brand is a subject.

brand.description: The brand record for authority.brand, from Brand Research. Descriptive, not authorising.

name.description: Display name, used as an exact lexical term.

aliases.description: Other spellings and product names, used as exact lexical terms.

parent.description: Owning company (Unilever for Dove). Recorded so the parent is never mistaken for the subject.

categories.description: Ranked, most applicable first. The first is the retrieval filter; the second is planned as a widening step. Leave empty rather than guess — the widening ladder handles a missing filter, it cannot un-guess a wrong one.

markets.description: Markets the brand operates in; joins the query text.

campaign.description: The campaign clan as key-value pairs. Keys not listed here are ACCEPTED and join the query text, so a campaign clan that grows a field degrades to 'still searchable' rather than 'rejected'.

campaign_type.description: Free text; mapped to effectiveness_type where the taxonomies share a concept, otherwise query text.

target.description: What is being generated with this context. The best evidence for an insight is not the best evidence for proof.

stage.description: Pipeline stage. Only the brief is served today.

field.description: The brief field being generated, when retrieval is per field.

text.description: Extracted text. Capped: this shapes a query, it is not the document store.

exclude_doc_ids.description: Documents that must not be returned for this run.

used_cites.description: Citations the model already has from an earlier call.

token_budget.description: Per-bucket token TARGETS, merged over the defaults. A target, not a wall — the top hit in a bucket is always kept.

latency_ms.description: Overall deadline for the RAG call.

target_model.description: The model that will read the context; caching minimums depend on it.

response.description: Structured, citable evidence — not a summary. The brief model synthesises; the RAG module selects, validates, orders and renders.

blocks.description: In prompt reading order. Hits within a block are in DELIVERED order, which may differ from score order once edge ordering is on.

prompt_text.description: The blocks rendered for a prompt, for callers that do not render their own.

notes.description: Plain-language warnings: unresolved filters, widening, fallbacks.

trace.description: brief_context.BriefContext.trace() — authorised vs served scopes and tenants, egress drops, per-hit scope. Log it per brief.

cite.description: Stable short id the model cites and check_grounding() verifies.

retrieval_score.description: Fused retrieval score. Rank-derived (RRF) — comparable within one query only, never a relevance probability.

weight.description: How much weight the model should give it. constraint = a human reviewer rejected this before; advice = textbook pitfalls; evidence = precedent, craft, standards.

relevance.description: The validation stage's verdict on this hit. null until that stage runs.

score.description: Calibrated backends only. A threshold is only ever compared against a non-null score.

backend.description: Which backend decided — recorded so a backend swap can be diffed rather than trusted.

validation.description: Run-level record of the validation stage. null until that stage runs.
